[raster] Clip the edge sweep's column walk to the surface (#6251)

* [raster] Clip the edge sweep's column walk to the surface

edge_sweep_row() walked every fixed-point pixel column an edge spans,
even though columns right of the surface contribute nothing and
columns left of it only contribute a cover delta that telescopes into
column 0.  A near-horizontal edge with extreme coordinates could span
~2^24 columns per row, making sweep cost proportional to coordinate
range instead of surface width: the ClusterFuzz testcase took 114s in
a plain release build.

Fold the left-of-surface portion of the walk into a single column-0
cover update, skip the right-of-surface portion, and enter/exit the
per-column loop at the visible window.  Jumping the incremental fy
accumulator by k*delta_fy is exact, since the increment is constant
and the running sums are bounded, so output is bit-identical; verified
by comparing 178 hb-raster renders (draw and paint paths, several
fonts, sizes, and negative-margin crops that clip edges off-surface)
byte-for-byte against the previous code.  The testcase now runs in
0.17s.  Also add it as a fuzz seed.

Fixes https://oss-fuzz.com/testcase-detail/5267980968329216

Assisted-by: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [raster] Keep an unclipped fast path in the edge sweep

The window clipping added in the previous commit made every
multi-column edge-row pay for the clip setup, measurable as ~1% more
instructions rasterizing all glyphs of NotoSansCJKsc/SourceHanSans-VF
at 256px with hb-raster-all.  Guard it with a two-compare check against
the stride-aligned column count (the same (width+3)&~3 pitch the image
row uses) and walk those edges with the original unclipped code.
cell_add() still drops columns past the logical width, so an edge that
only spills into the alignment padding takes the fast path without
changing coverage.  Auto-sized surfaces contain their visible edges;
this is the everyday case.

Interleaved perf-stat A/B (5 rounds, all glyphs at 256px): instruction
overhead drops to +0.24% (CJK) / +0.9% (AwamiNastaliq, tiny workload);
cycles flat to -1.3%, within noise.  Output remains bit-identical on
the 178-render comparison matrix, and the oss-fuzz 5267980968329216
testcase stays at 0.19s.

Assisted-by: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [raster] Charge column spans in the pixel-work estimate

hb_raster_draw_get_pixel_work() charged each edge only its scanline
span, so a nearly-horizontal edge crossing one pixel row but sweeping
the full surface width cost up to `width` cells while being charged 2
units — the paint path's pixel-budget precharge could undercharge the
sweep by a factor of the surface width.  This is the same blind spot
that let the previous commits' column-walk timeout through the paint
path's precharge.

Charge each edge its column span too, clipped to the surface width the
same way the row span is clipped to its height.  Since an edge is a
straight segment, row span plus clipped column span is a true upper
bound on the post-clipping sweep work.  Normal outlines are barely
affected: flattening yields short segments whose column spans are
commensurate with their row spans, far below the 2^26 budget.

No rendering change: the 178-render comparison matrix remains
bit-identical and the full test suite passes.

Assisted-by: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

[raster] Widen overflowing scanline accumulators (#6273)

The analytic rasterizer stored every row's area and cover in 32- and
16-bit accumulators. Highly overlapping outlines could exceed those
ranges and trigger signed overflow before coverage was clamped.

Keep compact SIMD accumulators for rows with at most 127 active edges.
Lazily use 64-bit scalar accumulators for denser rows, where the narrow
cover bound no longer holds. Add regressions for area overflow and
cover wrapping.

Tested with meson test -C build, the ASan/UBSan raster API test, all
raster fuzzer corpus chunks, and the supplied reproducer.

Assisted-by: OpenAI Codex <noreply@openai.com>

On the unclipped walk, store the cell directly.  Both endpoints were
already tested against the sweep window, so the per-cell reject only
adds a branch on the hot path.  Keep one scratch column past the
logical width for an edge that ends on the right pixel boundary — that
used to drop into the clip path — and do not paint it.  The draw object
is reused across extents, so size that row exactly instead of letting a
dirty resize retain the previous one.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

coupling: The overflow is the mismatch between two contracts that were edited in different commits. The clip commit lets the unclipped sweep visit every column of the stride pitch, raster_unclipped_columns() = (width+3)&~3, but cell_add() still drops columns at or past the logical width, so those extra visits do not store anything and the commit is safe on its own. The accumulator commit then stores that walk with cell_add_fast(), which has no column reject, and allocates the scratch row exactly width+1 so an edge ending on the right pixel boundary has one unpainted sentinel. Against the predicate that commit itself left in place (< width) every stored index fits in that row, so the commit is also safe on its own. Composed, an in-contract extent smaller than the ink takes the fast path whenever both endpoints fall in the pitch: width 1 and a line to x=2.5 visit columns 0, 1 and 2 (all < 4) and cell_add_fast() writes index 2 of a 2-element row. Fixing either diff on its own does not remove the bug. The clip diff is locally correct while cell_add() remains the store, so tightening it is not indicated by that diff; the accumulator diff is locally correct while the predicate is still < width, so growing the row past the one sentinel column is not indicated by that diff. Each edit only becomes an out-of-bounds write in the presence of the other. A repair has to notice that the predicate from the clip commit and the unchecked store from the accumulator commit no longer describe the same window.
